privacy.seoDescription: Cosmo's privacy policy: data collected, secure Supabase storage, Row Level Security, GDPR rights and contact.
privacy.title: Privacy policy

s1.title: 1. Data controller
s1.p1: The controller of the personal data collected through the Cosmo application is Axel Longatte, publisher of Cosmo, reachable at [contact@thecosmo.app](mailto:contact@thecosmo.app).

s2.title: 2. Data collected
s2.intro: While you use Cosmo, we collect only the data needed for the service to work:
s2.li1: **Identification data:** display name, email address, encrypted password (standard sign-up), or profile picture and Google identifier (sign-in through Google OAuth)
s2.li2: **Productivity data:** tasks, categories, lists, habits and their completion history, calendar events, OKRs (objectives and key results) and their progress
s2.li3: **Social data:** friend list, friend requests, tasks shared with other users
s2.li4: **Subscription data (business workspace):** the organisation's plan, subscription status and dates, and Stripe technical identifiers. Bank details are handled exclusively by Stripe; Cosmo has no access to them
s2.li5: **Technical data:** Supabase session information (authentication token, date of last sign-in) and the days on which you signed in (internal usage statistics)
s2.p1: **Audience measurement:** Cosmo uses Vesk, an audience measurement tool, loaded only if you accept it. For each page viewed it records the page address, the page you came from, your IP address, your browser, and engagement indicators (scroll depth, time spent, clicks on links and buttons). It builds no advertising profile.
s2.p2: **Measurement identifier:** Vesk stores a random identifier on your device, in your browser's local storage, which lets it recognise a single visit from one page to the next. It is not a cookie, but it is still information placed on your equipment: it is therefore written only after you accept, and it is erased as soon as you withdraw your consent with “Manage cookies”. Your IP address, your browser and this identifier are personal data. This data is not attached to your Cosmo account and is never cross-referenced with your tasks, habits or OKRs.
s2.p3: **Pages excluded from measurement:** audience measurement is never loaded on pages where you enter credentials (account creation, sign-in, password reset, accepting an invitation), nor on any screen of the application once you are signed in.
s2.note: No other third-party tracking tool (Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Hotjar, and so on) is used. Inside the application, nothing else is collected about your behaviour apart from the sign-in days described above.
s2.li6: **Business workspace data:** membership of an organisation, role, team tasks and projects, comments, activity history and notifications. For this data, the organisation is the controller and Cosmo acts on its behalf, as set out in section 6 of the Terms of Use
s2.li7: **Bug reports:** the message and any screenshots you attach, your account email address if you are signed in, and the technical context of the page, sent by email to the team
s2.li8: **Email invitations:** when a member of an organisation invites you, your email address is used to send you the invitation link, on behalf of that organisation. A link that is not accepted expires after 7 days and is erased 30 days later
s2.p4: **Where your sign-up came from:** if you accept it in the banner, Cosmo keeps for 30 days, in your browser's local storage, the channel that brought you here (the “ref” or “utm” parameter of a campaign link, or “demo”), then records it on your account if you create one. It is used only to know which channels bring sign-ups. Without your consent, nothing is stored or recorded.
s2.p5: **Trying the demo:** if you accept, a random device identifier is stored when you start the demo, and the visit is counted. If you then create an account from the same device, the visit is attached to your account, to measure how many trials lead to a sign-up. Without your consent, the demo works exactly the same and nothing is counted.

s3.title: 3. Authentication methods
s3.intro: Cosmo offers two ways to sign in:
s3.li1: **Email and password:** your password is hashed server-side by Supabase Auth and is never stored in clear text
s3.li2: **Google OAuth:** by signing in through Google, you authorise Cosmo to retrieve your name, email address and profile picture from your Google account. No access to your calendar or to any other Google service is requested

s4.title: 4. Purposes of processing
s4.intro: Your data is used solely to:
s4.li1: Create and authenticate your user account
s4.li2: Store and synchronise your productivity data (tasks, habits, calendar, OKRs)
s4.li3: Enable collaboration: task sharing, friend management and the business workspace
s4.li4: Process payments and manage the business workspace subscription
s4.li5: Keep the application secure and working properly
s4.li6: Produce internal usage statistics (sign-in days) and, with your consent, measure traffic and where sign-ups come from
s4.li7: Send you service emails: invitations, notices before a subscription renews, organisation notifications you chose to receive, replies to your messages

s5.title: 5. Legal basis
s5.intro: The processing of your data relies on:
s5.li1: **Performance of the contract**, for all data needed for the service to work
s5.li2: **Legitimate interest**, for the security and continuity of the application, and for internal usage statistics (sign-in days), which are used only to improve the service
s5.li3: **Consent**, for audience measurement (Vesk and Vercel Analytics), where your sign-up came from, counting demo trials, and anything stored on your device that is not strictly necessary to the service. Nothing is stored or loaded until you have accepted, and a refusal never stores anything. You can change your mind at any time
s5.note: Cosmo is intended for people aged at least 15. Below that age, audience measurement can only be accepted with the joint consent of a holder of parental authority (Article 45 of the French Data Protection Act).

s6.title: 6. Retention periods
s6.li1: Account and content data: kept while the account is active, then permanently deleted within 90 days of closure. An account with no sign-in for **3 years** is deleted, after a warning email sent 30 days beforehand
s6.li2: Session tokens: expire automatically according to the Supabase configuration
s6.li3: **Demo visit** (device identifier, stored only if you accepted): **90 days** if the visit does not lead to a sign-up, **400 days** if it does
s6.li4: **Activity days** (sign-in dates, used for usage statistics): **400 days**
s6.li5: **Technical payment markers** (identifiers of Stripe events already processed, used to avoid charging twice): **90 days**
s6.li6: Payment data: kept in line with legal obligations (10 years for accounting)
s6.note: These periods are applied automatically by the database, with no manual step. The payment journal is the exception: tax law requires it to be kept **and to remain unalterable**, so it can be neither erased nor modified, not even following a request to delete an account. Its rows contain neither your name nor your email address: they carry only a technical identifier, which stops designating anyone once your account is deleted.
s6.li7: **Where your sign-up came from** (only if you accepted): kept on your profile for as long as the account exists
s6.li8: **Bug reports**: the emails received are kept for at most 12 months after they have been handled
s6.li9: **Database backups**: encrypted, kept for 30 days, then replaced automatically

s7.title: 7. Data sharing
s7.intro: Your data may pass through the following processors:
s7.li1: **Supabase**: database and authentication. Your data is hosted in the **eu-west-1 (Ireland)** region, therefore within the European Union
s7.li2: **Vercel**: website hosting. Processes connection data (IP address, technical logs)
s7.li3: **Vercel Analytics**: cookie-free audience measurement, loaded only if you accept it
s7.li4: **Sentry**: technical error detection, data hosted in the Union (Germany). Email addresses and identifiers appearing in error messages are masked, and invitation or sign-in tokens are removed from page addresses. Your account's technical identifier (a random string, with no name or email) is attached to reports to link errors together
s7.li6: **Google**: only if you use Google OAuth sign-in
s7.li7: **Vesk** (a service of Veske, a sole trader established in France, hosted in Germany): audience measurement (page address, referring page, IP address, browser, engagement indicators, and a random identifier stored in the browser's local storage), loaded only if you accept it and never on pages where credentials are entered
s7.outro: No data is sold to third parties. Nothing is shared for advertising or marketing purposes.
s7.li8: **Resend**: sending service emails (bug reports, notices before a subscription renews)
s7.li9: **Cloudflare Turnstile**: bot protection on the sign-in and sign-up forms, when enabled. Processes your IP address and technical browser signals, with no advertising purpose
s7.li10: **GitHub**: storage of the daily database backups, encrypted before they are uploaded. GitHub does not hold the decryption key

s7bis.title: 7 bis. Transfers outside the European Union
s7bis.p1: Your database is hosted in Ireland, within the European Union.
s7bis.p2: However, several providers are companies established outside the Union or may access data from outside it: **Vercel**, **Sentry**, **Resend**, **Cloudflare**, **Stripe**, **Google** (Google sign-in), **GitHub** (encrypted backups), and **Supabase Inc.**, whose teams may access the infrastructure for maintenance and support. The data they process on our behalf may therefore be transferred outside the Union. These transfers are covered by the European Commission's adequacy decision on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, where the provider is certified under it, or otherwise by the Commission's standard contractual clauses (Articles 45 and 46 GDPR).
s7bis.p3: You can ask us for a copy of the applicable safeguards at the address given below.

s8.title: 8. Your rights (GDPR)
s8.intro: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you have the following rights:
s8.li1: **Right of access**: obtain a copy of your personal data
s8.li2: **Right to rectification**: correct inaccurate information from the settings
s8.li3: **Right to erasure**: delete your account and all your data
s8.li4: **Right to data portability**: export your data in a readable format
s8.li5: **Right to object**: object to certain processing
s8.li6: **Right to restriction**: restrict processing in certain cases
s8.p1: Portability is exercised directly from **Settings, My data tab**: the export covers your tasks, habits, events, OKRs, categories, lists and your profile, in CSV format.
s8.p2: For any other right: [contact@thecosmo.app](mailto:contact@thecosmo.app). We reply within **one month** of receiving your request, in accordance with Article 12 of the GDPR. That period may be extended by two months for a complex request, in which case we tell you within the first month.
s8.p3: You can also lodge a complaint with the **CNIL**, the French data protection authority: [www.cnil.fr](https://www.cnil.fr)
s8.li7: **Post-mortem instructions**: set instructions on how your data is kept, erased and disclosed after your death (Article 85 of the French Data Protection Act)

s9.title: 9. Security
s9.p1: All communications between your browser and our servers are encrypted with HTTPS/TLS. Passwords are stored hashed (bcrypt, through Supabase Auth). Access to data is protected by Row Level Security (RLS) policies in the database: each user can reach only their own data and what others have shared with them. The publisher has technical administrative access, reserved for maintenance, security and support. Database backups are encrypted.

s10.title: 10. Cookies and information stored on your device
s10.intro: The following are **strictly necessary** for the service to work, and are stored without your consent because the service cannot do without them:
s10.li2: Interface preferences stored in localStorage (theme, filters)
s10.li3: Your consent choice, stored in localStorage — it is what allows us to honour your refusal
s10.consentIntro: The following are stored **only after you accept**:
s10.consentLi1: A random identifier placed by Vesk in the browser's local storage, to recognise a single visit from one page to the next
s10.note1: No advertising cookie is placed on your device, and no data is used for advertising purposes.
s10.note2: Both of our audience measurement tools (Vesk and Vercel Analytics), where your sign-up came from and counting demo trials all require your consent: **none of this is loaded or stored until you click “Accept”** in the banner, and if you refuse, it never is. Your choice is kept on your device for six months, after which you are asked again. You can change it at any time with the button below or the “Manage cookies” link: if you withdraw your consent, the identifiers and sign-up origin stored on your device are erased.
s10.consentLi2: Where your sign-up came from (campaign link or demo), kept for 30 days in the browser's local storage
s10.consentLi3: A random device identifier stored when the demo starts, to count trials
s10.consentLi4: Two demo counters (time spent and number of items created), which choose when to suggest an account. Without your consent, they stay in memory and disappear when the page is reloaded

s11.title: 11. Changes
s11.p1: This policy may be updated. In the event of a substantial change, you will be informed by email or through a notification in the application. The date of the last update is shown at the top of this page.

s12.title: 12. Language of this document
s12.p1: This document is available in French and in English. **If the two versions differ, the French version prevails**: it is the original version.
